significance: The Theravada temple on the artificial hill from which Phnom Penh takes its name, traditionally founded in 1372 by the woman known as Lady Penh and rebuilt repeatedly through the nineteenth century and again in 1926. King Ponhea Yat moved the Cambodian capital here in 1397 and a large stupa was later raised for him at the summit; the hill and sanctuary together stand 46 metres high, and the shrine holds four Buddha images and one of Vishnu.
story: Lady Penh is said to have gone down to the river in the rain to bathe and found a floating koki tree carrying five statues, which she housed in a shrine built on a mound raised for the purpose.
